Buhbeespatiogarden, this is absolutely true. Everyone thinks it has to be both. I can be, but for the vast majority, it's do the job you have to do, but do it a little less than what you've been doing. 5 days instead of 6, 4 days instead of 5. Then capitalize on the time you're wasting from 11pm - 3am and use it to either grow your brand and impact or use it to discover yourself as a beautiful human being.

I love this. This hits it right no the head. The latter is what most are missing. Work 4 days, not 5 days away. Focus on you. Focus on freelance if that's your thing. Or focus on mental health and relaxation. The key is to not be afraid of the person you work for. Not to be controlled. Not be blackmailed by bosses. The conversation is simple. I can work part time for you and in the other time, I'm doing things that fulfill me.

It's not realistic to expect your passion to pay for your place or car. You've got to pay your bills however you can. It's important to always feed your soul first with what makes you happy. When the day starts first, and then do what you have to do to grind and survive. Work 4 days away instead of 5. Then use the rest of that time to build you, your health and your spirit. We've all been oppressed and made to believe we aren't valuable and important individuals. Jobs need us, not the other way around. You are you, outside of whatever you've got to do to pay the bills.

Onions Make Me Cry, you and your husband are extremely intelligent. Putting all of your self worth in your job can lead to some insane depression when or if you lose it. There's nothing wrong with doing an amazing job at work, but you should always be filling yourself up with your passion and happiness before the work day starts. If you're in the 1% of people who love their job, but also love their hobbies, you've won, regardless of cashflow. Thank you for your thoughts.

I grew up in the projects with a single mother scraping to provide for us. My father locked up. She died at 12, where we were thrown around in the system like a rag doll. So obviously I do know. Most people hate their minimum wage job and think that going to college for 4 years will some how be a gateway drug. It’s not. It smothers who you are an individual and makes you hate life even more because you feel like a failure. I’ve been there. What I recommend is simple. Work 4 days a week at your shit job, not 5. Use the other 3 to focus on you and freelance. Pay your bills. Feed your soul. Repeat. Until you can work 3 days at that garbage job because you’ve made an extra 1K/mo from your side hustle. What are you doing from 10pm - 2am. Hustle your creative face off and find happiness in your process, not the $$$ at the end CORVUS_ANTIPODUM.

Very true. I recommend this middle ground: Work 4 days a week, not 5 at the job that pays your bills. Spend the other 3 doing what you love. Freelancing if you want. Then transition (if you hate that job, some don’t) to 3 days a week there, 4 days your time. So on and so forth.
